structure.title: I. Background (Nigerian oil sector; offshoring and divestment)
V. Main Results, A-C (main outcomes, output decomposition, other outcomes)
VII. Welfare Analysis (government revenue and welfare accounting)

observations.statement: States the estimand as the effect of local firm participation (indigenization) on field-level performance, identified through a staggered-adoption two-way fixed effects difference-in-differences comparing fields that change local ownership status to fields whose ownership status does not change.
observations.locator: Section IV, equation for baseline TWFE model

observations.statement: Argues identification requires no differential trends in unobserved field quality correlated with the timing of divestment, conditional on fixed effects, and states that adverse selection by incumbent multinationals would if anything bias results against finding a local advantage.

Identifies selection of assets into divestment based on unobserved trends as the primary identification threat and motivates why the institutional process governing asset sales limits the ability of market participants to manipulate the exact timing of ownership change.
observations.quote: the exact timing of local take-over is not directly manipulable

observations.statement: Names the baseline design as a two-way fixed effects staggered-adoption difference-in-differences, complemented by a stacked event-study specification, and states that alternative estimators addressing treatment-effect heterogeneity are examined separately as diagnostics.

Defines the unit of observation as the field-year and builds the panel by combining administrative production and licensing records with an environmental agency's spill and theft reports, a conflict-event database, and a commercial transactions database.

Describes the working sample as an unbalanced panel that begins in the mid-2000s, explaining that a field enters when it first appears in administrative production records and remains in the panel thereafter even in years when output is missing.

Notes that some outcome variables are available only for narrower time windows or firm subsets than the main output and theft measures, for example enforcement events, gas flaring, and political connections, so table-specific samples are smaller than the core panel.

States that biographical data on corporate officers were assembled with a commercial research partner from corporate filings and that some individuals could not be matched to biographical records, so the connections analysis covers less than the full identified roster.

Constructs the local-participation treatment as a binary indicator built from the earlier of two independently sourced take-over dates, coded to switch on permanently in the year of first local participation, consistent with a staggered-adoption design.

Defines the primary outcomes from investigative and administrative records: legal output as production reported for royalty purposes net of losses, theft as spills attributed to third-party sabotage, and non-sabotage spills as a proxy for operational quality.

Discusses two candidate sources of measurement error in the outcome data, output underreporting for royalty avoidance and misclassification of spill cause, and reports external validation checks against trade data and independently audited spill records before treating the measures as reliable.

Reports that a supplementary instrumental-variables specification, detailed in the appendix, is used to separate the estimated output effect into a component recouped from the black market and a component representing new production.

Reports the main table with field and year fixed effects as the baseline column, then adds interacted geographic controls, field-specific time trends, and progressively finer state-by-year and locality-by-year fixed effects in successive columns.
States that the control-group mean of the dependent variable, the observation count, and R-squared are reported beneath the coefficient rows for every panel of the main and heterogeneity tables.
States in the notes beneath every regression table that standard errors are clustered, specifying the clustering unit directly under the table rather than only in the running text.
observations.locator: Table 1 notes and similarly for Tables 2-7

observations.statement: Follows a baseline-then-variants layout throughout the paper's tables, presenting an unadorned two-way fixed effects column first and then adding controls or richer fixed effects in later columns, without any column reporting regression weights.
observations.note: No table reports weights; treated as absence rather than an explicit statement, recorded also in gaps.

observations.statement: States that standard errors are clustered at the field level throughout the main specifications, matching the level at which the treatment indicator varies over time.

Reports an appendix robustness exercise that recomputes inference using spatial standard errors at several radii, alongside alternative clustering levels, motivated by the fact that outcomes are defined within a fixed distance of the field centroid and could be spatially correlated across nearby fields.

Does not state an explicit multiple-testing correction anywhere in the text despite reporting results for many outcome variables and running a large combinatorial set of specifications summarized in a single robustness figure.
Reports dynamic stacked event-study estimates for the main outcomes directly in the main text and discusses the pre-period coefficients there as the parallel trends check.

Uses divestment deals that were announced but ultimately stalled or terminated as a placebo group, treating the announcement date as a pseudo-event and reporting no systematic pattern around it as evidence against selection on unobserved trends.

Presents a table comparing time-invariant and initial time-varying characteristics of divested fields against always-treated and never-treated groups, both unconditionally and after conditioning on onshore location, and uses the comparison to argue for a preferred control group.
observations.locator: Section II.D, Supplemental Appendix Table A4

observations.statement: States that formal diagnostics for bias from staggered treatment timing under two-way fixed effects, including a decomposition of the estimator into comparison-group weights and a group-time robust estimator, are carried out in the appendix rather than the main tables.

Summarizes robustness across a large combinatorial set of control, shock-control, interacted fixed-effect, treatment-definition, and sample choices in a single specification-curve figure showing ordered coefficients with confidence intervals alongside a distribution of t-statistics.

States that robustness to alternative difference-in-differences estimators designed to address heterogeneous treatment-effect bias is examined in an appendix section and narratively concludes that these alternatives do not change the main conclusions.

Reports a table that separates transactions between two local firms and other non-localizing transactions from the main multinational-to-local divestment indicator, functioning as a within-sample check that the comparison group is not driving the result.

States that outcome measurement is tested against alternative distance radii and field-boundary polygons, and that inference is tested against alternative clustering levels and spatially correlated standard errors, all reported in an appendix table.

Splits the sample into onshore and offshore assets, motivated ex ante by the theoretical model's prediction that the security-driven local advantage should be concentrated onshore where political risk is higher, while the quality disadvantage should be larger offshore where technology requirements are higher.

Separately estimates the association between field outcomes and security-affiliated political connections versus other political connections, treating the contrast between the two connection types as informative about the proposed mechanism rather than as a general test of political-connection value.
Expresses the main effect estimates as a share of the control-group mean of the dependent variable throughout the results discussion, rather than relying on levels alone to convey magnitude.

Converts the regression-based revenue and welfare estimates into a back-of-envelope monetary aggregate over the sample period and expresses the resulting figures as shares of the oil sector and of national GDP.

Benchmarks measurement choices and valuation assumptions against external sources, including validating reported output against trading-partner export data and pricing deferred production using historical differences between high- and low-theft price periods.

Explicitly flags that the confidence interval around part of the output-gain decomposition cannot rule out a null new-output effect, and structures the welfare exercise around multiple named scenarios in response to this imprecision rather than reporting a single point estimate.
States that firm-level cost or productivity data are unavailable, so the quality disadvantage of local firms is inferred only indirectly through the oil-spill outcome rather than measured directly.

States that several welfare components, including policing costs and productivity or cost differentials between firm types, are unobserved and therefore excluded from the calculation, so the reported welfare gain is presented explicitly as an upper bound.

Frames the welfare exercise as conditional on the existing corruption and weak-institution environment, explicitly distinguishing the estimated gains from a first-best or globally optimal policy comparison.
observations.locator: Section VII.B and Section VIII Conclusion

observations.statement: Closes by arguing the Nigerian oil sector is not a special case but representative of extractive settings elsewhere characterized by black markets, organized crime, and weak institutions, while the empirical evidence itself is drawn from a single country and sector.
Displays dynamic treatment effects as stacked event-study coefficient plots with confidence bands across relative event time for both the main outcomes and the enforcement and connections outcomes.

Organizes the summary statistics table by always-treated, divested, and never-treated groups, reporting means and standard deviations alongside unconditional and onshore-conditioned mean differences between the treated and comparison groups.
observations.locator: Section II.D, Supplemental Appendix Table A4

observations.statement: Restates the sample definition, outcome construction, control variable list, and standard-error clustering level in the notes beneath each main regression table rather than requiring the reader to consult the main text.

Presents the large-scale specification-robustness exercise as an ordered coefficient plot with confidence intervals paired with a companion panel showing the distribution of t-statistics across specifications.

Previews the paper's main findings on output, theft, mechanisms, and welfare in sequence within the introduction before the formal empirical sections are presented, effectively serving as a roadmap for the reader.

Places the institutional background and data description sections before the theoretical model and the formal empirical-strategy section, so data sources and institutional context are established before the identification equation is introduced.

Groups falsification and robustness tests into a dedicated subsection at the close of the main-results section, structurally separate from the subsequent mechanisms section that follows the primary reduced-form estimates.

Repeatedly defers derivations, additional tables, and extended robustness exercises to a supplemental appendix referenced throughout the data, design, results, mechanism, and welfare sections, while the introduction contains an explicit paragraph positioning the paper's contribution relative to two literatures.

Tests the proposed law-enforcement mechanism using an intermediate outcome, counts of anti-theft enforcement actions built from media reports, rather than relying only on the ultimate output and theft outcomes.
Uses the contrast between security-affiliated and other political connections, rather than a pooled political-connections measure, as the evidentiary basis for the proposed corruption channel.

Works through several alternative explanations in a dedicated subsection, including spatial spillovers, dynamic extraction paths, community grievance, local economic spillovers, targeted corporate investment, and collusion with armed groups, reporting evidence against each and explicitly labeling some of this evidence as suggestive.

Tests for local economic spillovers using a national household panel survey linked to the nearest oil field, rather than relying only on administrative field-level records for this alternative-mechanism check.

Directs readers in a title-page footnote to the article's online landing page for additional materials and the author disclosure statement rather than describing a data or code deposit directly within the main text.
observations.quote: additional materials and author disclosure statement(s)

observations.statement: Draws core datasets from administrative government records, a paid market-intelligence transactions database, and a commissioned partnership with a corporate research firm for biographical data, rather than from a single public microdata source.

concordance.paper_says: Baseline model is a two-way fixed effects OLS regression of field outcomes on a local-participation indicator with field and year fixed effects, clustered by field.
concordance.card_shows: Spec s1 uses reghdfe (hdfe_ols) with absorb(fcode year), cl(fcode), matching the baseline TWFE model.

concordance.paper_says: Reports additional columns with field-specific linear time trends and with state-by-year and locality-by-year fixed effects beyond the field and year baseline.
concordance.card_shows: Only the baseline field/year fixed effects (s1) and a controls-by-year interacted family (s2) were recorded from the sampled code ranges; state-by-year and locality-by-year variants are not separately captured.

concordance.paper_says: States standard errors are clustered at the field level throughout the main specifications.
concordance.card_shows: se.cluster_level is fcode (field) for specs s1, s2, and s5.

concordance.paper_says: States standard errors are clustered (not heteroskedasticity-robust only) in every main table.
concordance.card_shows: se.type is cluster for s1, s2, and s5.

concordance.paper_says: Names the control variables explicitly as field latitude, distance to the state capital, distance to the nearest river, and distance to the coast.
concordance.card_shows: controls_summary is null in s1 and s2; the Stata call absorbs a macro '$controls' whose contents were not resolved from the sampled code ranges.

concordance.paper_says: Does not mention any regression weighting scheme in the empirical strategy or table notes.
concordance.card_shows: weights is null (unknown) for the recorded specifications.

concordance.paper_says: Describes the comparison group as fields whose ownership status does not change, that is always-treated and never-treated fields, with a data-driven argument for preferring never-treated fields.
concordance.card_shows: comparison_group is null for the recorded design and specifications.

concordance.paper_says: States the analysis sample is an unbalanced field-year panel over an eleven-year window described in Section II.
concordance.card_shows: pipeline sample_restrictions record a year-range filter applied in the cleaning script, consistent with the stated panel window.

concordance.paper_says: Reports a dynamic stacked event-study figure in the main text described as showing flat pre-period coefficients for the main outcomes.
concordance.card_shows: Diagnostic x1 (pretrend_test) is recorded as not_found_in_scope in the sampled files, with a note that the event-study plot serves as the only located pre-trend check.

concordance.paper_says: States that alternative difference-in-differences estimators addressing staggered-timing bias, including a group-time robust estimator and a decomposition of the TWFE coefficient, are used as appendix robustness checks.
concordance.card_shows: Spec s3 (csdid, Callaway-Sant'Anna group-time ATT) and spec s4 (bacondecomp) are both present in the appendix do-file, and diagnostic x2 confirms the group-time estimator's heterogeneous-effects output.

concordance.paper_says: Organizes results into eight main numbered tables and five main numbered figures, each tied to a specific claim in the text.
concordance.card_shows: outputs.tables and outputs.figures are both empty; the card does not map specifications to specific table or figure numbers.

concordance.paper_says: Names multiple distinct data sources by provider, including a national oil company and petroleum resources department, an oil-spill investigation agency, a conflict-event database, a commercial transactions database, and a corporate research partner.
concordance.card_shows: The data array contains a single generic entry (field_panel_all) with source_hint null, without enumerating the underlying source providers.

gaps: No explicit preregistration, pre-analysis plan, or IRB/ethics statement was found anywhere in the main text or footnotes.
No statistical software (e.g., Stata, R) is named anywhere in the visible article text; software choice is only inferable from the separately reviewed replication code.
No explicit multiple-hypothesis-testing correction is discussed despite many outcome variables and a large combinatorial specification-robustness exercise.
No discussion of a few-clusters problem is present despite field-level clustering being the sole reported inference approach in the main tables.

The paper's Supplemental Appendix A through H, referenced extensively for data construction, model derivation, and additional tables and figures, is a separate online document not included in the provided text and could not be read.
No table or specification states regression weights; the absence itself is not discussed.

reading.note: Read the full introduction, background, data, theoretical framework, empirical strategy, main results, robustness, mechanisms, welfare, and conclusion sections (pages 1-34) in full. Pages 35-39 (References) were skimmed only to confirm section boundaries and were not read in detail. The paper's Supplemental Appendix A-H, cross-referenced dozens of times for data construction detail, model derivations, and additional tables/figures, is a separate online document not contained in this PDF/text and was not available to read.
